newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN TV SOLVES MATCH RIGHTS DISPUTE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN TV SOLVES MATCH RIGHTS DISPUTE.

text.p: Three million viewers who risked missing a key World Cup qualifier between England and Italy breathed a sigh of relief on Wednesday when a last-minute deal was clinched over disputed broadcast rights.

Private network TeleMonteCarlo (TMC), which won the rights to show the game live but whose signal covers only 80 percent of Italy, said it had reached a deal with state broadcaster RAI to show a taped version of the match at midnight local time.
TMC made the announcement in a live broadcast from London about two hours before kick-off at Wembley stadium.
It said RAI would not pay to show the match, adding that it had simply asked the state company to make a donation of its choice to two Florentine charities.

Earlier, the government had tried to find a way for the entire country to see the match but the efforts failed when RAI refused to pay TMC eight billion lire ($4.9 million) to show a taped version of the game.
Italian defender Fabio Cannavaro had said his parents did not receive TMC in their home in Naples and would go to a friend's house to watch the match.
